name: Sheet-pan chicken fajitas
tip: Set everything in the middle of the table and let everyone build their own.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slice chicken and peppers into strips.
Toss chicken and peppers with oil, fajita seasoning, salt and pepper.

Roast for 20–22 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through in the thickest part. Before serving, cut into the thickest piece: it should be steaming hot throughout with no pink meat, and the juices should run clear. If unsure, continue cooking. Spread the seasoned ingredients across the tray rather than piling them up so the edges roast golden.
Finish with lime off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
Warm wraps and serve with grated cheddar and soured cream.

name: Creamy garlic parmesan chicken pasta
tip: A deep pan keeps washing-up to a minimum.
method: Dice chicken and sauté in a little oil until lightly golden. Add garlic.

Add penne and hot chicken stock. Simmer, stirring often, until pasta is nearly tender; add a splash of water if needed. Reserve a little starchy cooking water, then toss the pasta and sauce together until the coating is glossy rather than watery.

Finish with lemon off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
Turn off the heat, stir through parmesan and season to taste.

name: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled pork buns
tip: Start it in the morning and dinner practically takes care of itself.
method: Before switching on the slow cooker, pat the pork shoulder dry. Rub the whole joint with smoked paprika and crushed garlic, then set it on the sliced onion; add the BBQ sauce and apple cider vinegar around the meat. Slow-cook the joint whole rather than cutting it into cubes.

Slice the onion. Put the 1.2 kg pork shoulder in the slow cooker with the onion and about 150 ml BBQ sauce. Add 100 ml water if the cooker needs a little liquid; consult its instructions. Leave the whole joint intact while it slow-cooks and test for fork-tenderness before shredding into its reduced juices.
Cook on low for 7–8 hours, until tender and safely cooked.
Shred with two forks and stir through the cooking juices.
Once the shoulder pulls apart easily, shred it into its cooking juices and simmer the sauce uncovered briefly if it needs thickening before piling into buns.
Fill six brioche buns with shredded pork and divide the 300 g prepared coleslaw between them. Serve extra BBQ sauce only if separately purchased.

name: Beef & three-bean chilli
tip: Make extra and freeze portions for an easy future dinner.
method: Brown beef mince with diced onion and garlic. Drain excess fat if needed.

Add cumin, smoked paprika and chilli powder, then stir in one 400 g tin of chopped tomatoes and beans drained and rinsed from two 400 g tins (about 480 g drained in total). Cook the spices with the vegetables until fragrant, then let the rice absorb the seasoned stock until tender and separate.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Ensure mince is thoroughly cooked.

Cook 450 g dry rice (75 g per serving) following packet instructions while the chilli simmers. Serve the chilli over the cooked rice, with soured cream if desired. Keep the remaining dry rice from the purchased bag for another meal.
Finish with lime off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
The rice is listed as 450 g dry measured from a 1 kg purchased bag, not 1 kg cooked in this meal. Make sure the beef mince is thoroughly cooked before serving.

name: Honey-soy salmon & greens
tip: A sweet-savoury glaze does all the heavy lifting.
method: Finely grate the fresh ginger, crush the garlic, and whisk them with the honey, soy sauce and sesame oil to make a glossy glaze. Pat the salmon dry; keep most of the glaze for basting toward the end.
Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Place salmon and broccoli on a lined tray. Give the glaze its final two minutes under close watch, spooning over the juices so it turns glossy without burning.
Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp runny honey and two minced garlic cloves; brush the sauce over the four salmon fillets. Toss the 400 g broccoli with a spoonful of the sauce, if desired.
Bake for 12–18 minutes, depending on thickness, until salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Spoon the bubbling tray juices over the salmon for the final 2 minutes, watching the honey so it caramelises rather than burns. Finish off the heat with fresh lime juice.
Serve salmon and greens together; rice or potatoes are optional extra purchases, not included in this recipe’s ingredient estimate.

name: Tomato butter bean stew
tip: A warming bowl of tomato butter bean stew with butter beans at its heart.
method: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic. Wash the spinach.

Warm 1 tbsp oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5–6 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds without browning. Soften the vegetable base first, then simmer gently until the broth tastes rounded and the sauce has body.
Finely chop or grate the fresh parsley and add with the softened aromatics so their fragrance runs through the sauce.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the butter beans and simmer uncovered for another 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Fold in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, about 2 minutes. Taste and season. Serve with bread once the beans are piping hot and the sauce coats a spoon.

name: Baked bean cheese toasties
tip: Oven-baked baked bean cheese toasties with baked beans for a hearty, hands-off dinner.
method: Grate the cheddar, lightly butter the outside of each bread slice and drain a little sauce from the beans if very wet.
Heat the beans in a saucepan for 3–4 minutes, stirring until piping hot. Spoon onto the unbuttered sides of half the bread and scatter cheddar over them.

Close with the remaining slices, buttered sides facing out. Cook in a sandwich press or covered frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side. Leave space between the ingredients so hot air reaches the edges and they roast golden rather than steaming.
Check that the bread is crisp and golden and the cheese fully melted. Let the toasties stand for a minute before cutting; the filling will be very hot.

name: Creamy mushroom pasta
tip: Comforting creamy mushroom pasta with mushrooms — just the thing for a cosy supper.
method: Cook the sliced mushrooms in a wide, hot pan until their liquid evaporates and their edges turn golden before adding garlic.
Slice the mushrooms, mince the garlic and bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

Cook pasta according to the packet until just tender. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining. Reserve a little starchy cooking water, then toss the pasta and sauce together until the coating is glossy rather than watery.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide frying pan. Cook mushrooms over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid evaporates and they brown. Add garlic for 30 seconds.
Loosen the cream cheese sauce with pasta water and finish with a squeeze of lemon off the heat.
Lower the heat and stir in cream cheese with a splash of pasta water to make a smooth sauce. Toss with pasta, adding more water as needed. Serve when hot and creamy.

name: Crispy potato and egg hash
tip: A satisfying crispy potato and egg hash with potatoes to start the day.
method: Dust the diced potatoes with smoked paprika and pan-fry without stirring too often so a proper crust forms.
Cut potatoes into roughly 1 cm cubes so they cook evenly. Dice onion and peppers and pat potatoes dry.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Cook potatoes for 12–18 minutes, turning every few minutes, until golden and easily pierced with a fork.
Add onion and peppers and cook for another 5–6 minutes until softened. Make four small spaces in the hash.
Crack in the eggs only after the potatoes are crisp and the peppers have softened. Leave space between the ingredients so hot air reaches the edges and they roast golden rather than steaming.
Crack an egg into each space. Cover and cook gently for 3–6 minutes until the whites are set; cook yolks to a safe doneness for your diners. Season and serve hot.

name: Sausage and bean casserole
tip: Bring sausage and bean casserole to the table with sausages and cannellini beans.
method: Brown the sausages well first, then let smoked paprika bloom briefly with the softened onion before pouring in passata.
Slice sausages into bite-sized pieces and dice the onion. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.

Brown sausage pieces in a deep pan over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, turning to colour all sides. Add onion and cook for another 4 minutes. Soften the vegetable base first, then simmer gently until the broth tastes rounded and the sauce has body.
Add passata, 250 ml stock and beans. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Simmer with the beans until the tomato sauce is thick enough to coat the sausages.

Check sausage pieces are thoroughly cooked in the centre and the sauce is thickened. Taste and season before serving. Before serving, cut into the centre of the largest piece: the meat should be steaming hot all the way through, fully cooked and not pink. If unsure, continue cooking.

name: Chickpea tomato shakshuka
tip: Bring chickpea tomato shakshuka to the table with chickpeas and eggs.
method: Soften the peppers, then briefly fry ground cumin and crushed garlic until fragrant before adding the tomatoes and chickpeas.
Drain chickpeas, dice the peppers and pour the chopped tomatoes into a jug. Crack each egg into a separate small cup.

Warm a little oil in a lidded frying pan. Cook peppers over medium heat for 5–6 minutes until softened. Add tomatoes and chickpeas. Give the first side time to turn golden before stirring; a crowded pan steams instead of sears.
Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Make four wells and carefully slide an egg into each.
Make small wells in the thickened sauce for the eggs and cook until the whites have set.
Cover and cook on low for 5–8 minutes, checking that the whites have set; cook yolks appropriately for the diners. Serve straight from the pan.

name: Broccoli cheddar baked rice
tip: Oven-baked broccoli cheddar baked rice with rice for a hearty, hands-off dinner.
method: Whisk a little Dijon mustard into the warm milk-and-stock mixture before pouring it over rice and broccoli.

Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook rice according to its packet, then drain if needed. Cut broccoli into small florets and grate cheddar. Leave space between the ingredients so hot air reaches the edges and they roast golden rather than steaming.
Steam or boil broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then drain well. Warm the milk and 150 ml vegetable stock together.
Combine rice, broccoli and warm liquid in a baking dish. Scatter cheddar evenly over the surface.
Bake until the rice is tender, the liquid absorbed and the cheddar topping bubbling and golden.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until bubbling and lightly golden. Check the centre is piping hot; rest for 3 minutes before serving.

name: Greek chicken protein bowls
tip: Bring greek chicken protein bowls to the table with chicken breast and rice.
method: Cook rice according to the packet. Cut chicken into even strips, dice tomatoes and cucumber, and keep the raw chicken away from the salad.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Season chicken and cook for 6–9 minutes, turning, until golden and fully cooked in the thickest part. Before serving, cut into the thickest piece: it should be steaming hot throughout with no pink meat, and the juices should run clear. If unsure, continue cooking.

Rest chicken for 2–3 minutes. Stir a little water and seasoning into the Greek yoghurt for a pourable dressing. Dress the fresh elements just before serving so the herbs stay bright and the vegetables hold their crunch.
Finish with lemon off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
Divide rice into bowls, top with chicken, cucumber and tomatoes, then spoon over yoghurt. Use clean utensils for the ready-to-eat salad.

name: Cottage cheese egg muffins

method: Finely chop parsley and fold into the whisked eggs and cottage cheese with diced peppers for a fresh savoury note.

Whisk eggs in a bowl until combined. Stir in cottage cheese, vegetables and a pinch of seasoning.

name: Chocolate brownies
tip: A rich chocolate bake with a crackly top and fudgy centre; cool before cutting for neat squares.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin with parchment.
Melt the butter with dark chocolate gently; cool for a few minutes.
Whisk sugar and eggs together for 2 minutes, then stir in the melted chocolate.

Cool fully in the tin before slicing into nine squares. Store chilled if adding a dairy topping.

name: Sticky toffee pudding
tip: Soft date sponge with warm toffee sauce; delicious with vanilla ice cream. Preparation and baking take around 55 minutes.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a six-portion muffin tin or a small 20 cm baking dish.
Cover the chopped dates with 180 ml boiling water, leave 10 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda and mash until soft.

Cream 75 g of butter with 100 g of brown sugar; beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and date mixture. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, or until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
For the sauce, gently simmer the remaining 35 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, cream and golden syrup for 3–5 minutes until glossy.
Serve the warm sponge with toffee sauce and ice cream. Refrigerate any dairy leftovers promptly.

name: Lemon drizzle cake
tip: A buttery lemon sponge soaked with citrus syrup and finished with a simple glaze.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat softened butter with 160 g caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder and finely grated zest of two lemons; loosen with the milk. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Warm the juice of two lemons with the remaining 40 g caster sugar; prick the warm loaf and pour over.
When cool, mix icing sugar with enough juice from the third lemon to make a thick drizzle and spoon over the cake.

name: Rice pudding

name: Carrot cake

method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan); line a 20 cm round cake tin with parchment.
Whisk oil, eggs and brown sugar, then fold in flour, cinnamon and mixed spice. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Grate carrots finely and fold them into the batter with chopped walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40–50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean; cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, softened butter and icing sugar into a smooth icing; avoid overbeating.
Spread icing on the cooled cake, sprinkle with extra walnuts if desired and refrigerate until serving.

name: Jam roly-poly
tip: Traditional rolled suet sponge with raspberry jam; bake wrapped in parchment and foil.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and set a deep roasting tray of water on the lowest shelf.
Mix flour, suet and sugar, then stir in milk gradually to make a soft but not sticky dough. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Roll on a floured surface into a roughly 25 x 30 cm rectangle; spread jam, leaving a 2 cm border.
Roll up from a short edge, pinch the seam and ends closed, and wrap loosely in buttered baking parchment then foil to allow expansion.
Place the parcel seam-side down on a baking tray and bake for 45–55 minutes until the sponge is cooked through.
Unwrap carefully to avoid hot steam, cut into thick slices and serve with warm custard.

name: Tiramisu
tip: Coffee-soaked sponge with mascarpone cream. This version avoids raw eggs and alcohol; allow four hours to chill.
method: Brew strong coffee and let it cool completely.
Whisk mascarpone, icing sugar and vanilla until just smooth.
In another bowl whip the cold cream to soft peaks, then fold it gently into the mascarpone. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Dip each sponge finger briefly into the cold coffee and line the bottom of a 20 cm square dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the sponge, then repeat with another coffee-dipped layer and remaining cream.
Cover and chill for at least four hours or overnight.
Dust with cocoa and grate dark chocolate over the top just before serving. Keep refrigerated.

name: Lemon cheesecake
tip: Zesty no-bake lemon cheesecake; refrigerate at least four hours before slicing.
method: Line the base of a 20 cm springform cake tin with baking parchment.
Crush biscuits to fine crumbs; mix with melted butter, press into the tin and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat cream cheese with icing sugar, vanilla and finely grated lemon zest until smooth.

Whisk cold cream to soft peaks, then gently fold into the cream-cheese mixture with 3–4 tbsp fresh lemon juice. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Spoon onto biscuit base, level and refrigerate at least four hours until firm.
Remove carefully from the tin and garnish with extra lemon zest; keep refrigerated until serving.

name: Chocolate profiteroles
tip: Crisp choux buns filled with whipped cream and finished with warm chocolate sauce.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two trays.

Bring 250 ml water and butter to the boil in a saucepan; immediately add all the flour and beat vigorously until the dough forms a ball. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs gradually until the paste is glossy and holds its shape.
Pipe or spoon 18 small mounds onto trays; bake 25–30 minutes until deep golden and dry. Do not open the oven early.
Pierce each bun to release steam, then cool completely on a rack.
Whip cold cream with icing sugar and vanilla; split the buns and fill just before serving.
Melt chocolate gently with milk and caster sugar, drizzle over the filled profiteroles and serve immediately.

name: Treacle tart
tip: A classic British golden-syrup tart, best served warm with cream or custard.
method: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin with pastry and trim the edges.

Prick the base, line with baking paper and baking beans, then blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and bake for another 5 minutes. Check near the end for set edges and the intended texture, then cool before slicing so the finish stays neat.
Warm golden syrup gently to make it easier to pour; mix in breadcrumbs, lemon zest and juice, ground ginger and beaten egg.
Pour the mixture into the pastry shell and dot with the butter.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and set but still slightly soft in the middle.
Leave 15 minutes before slicing and serve with lightly whipped double cream.

name: Creamy chicken and broccoli pasta bake
tip: Comforting creamy chicken and broccoli pasta bake with dried pasta — just the thing for a cosy supper.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook pasta 2 minutes less than packet instructions; add broccoli for the final 3 minutes, then drain. Reserve a little starchy cooking water, then toss the pasta and sauce together until the coating is glossy rather than watery.
Finely chop or grate the garlic and add with the softened aromatics so their fragrance runs through the sauce.

Heat oil in a frying pan and cook diced chicken until browned and thoroughly cooked in the centre. Before serving, cut into the thickest piece: it should be steaming hot throughout with no pink meat, and the juices should run clear. If unsure, continue cooking.
In a saucepan, melt butter, stir in flour for 1 minute, then whisk in milk gradually until thickened. Stir in half the cheese and herbs.
Mix pasta, broccoli, chicken and sauce in a baking dish. Sprinkle over remaining cheese.
Finish with lemon off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
Bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Mini cottage pies with peas
tip: Bring mini cottage pies with peas to the table with lean beef mince and onion.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil potatoes in water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with butter and milk. Leave space between the ingredients so hot air reaches the edges and they roast golden rather than steaming.
Heat oil in a large pan. Soften onion and carrots for 5 minutes. Add mince and cook until browned, breaking up lumps.
Stir in tomato purée and stock. Simmer 12–15 minutes until the sauce thickens, then stir in peas.
Divide filling between four oven-safe dishes, top with mash and rough up with a fork.
Bake 15–20 minutes until the tops are golden and filling is piping hot. Cool slightly for children.

name: Classic banana bread
tip: A proper two-pound loaf: spotty bananas make the best slices.
method: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g/2 lb loaf tin with baking parchment.
Mash the peeled bananas in a large bowl. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Whisk eggs, sugar, melted butter and vanilla into the mashed banana.

Fold in self-raising flour, baking powder and cinnamon just until no dry flour remains; do not overmix. Once the flour is added, fold gently just until no dry pockets remain so the crumb stays tender.
Spoon into the lined tin and bake for 55–65 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out without wet batter. Cover loosely with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then move to a rack for at least 10 minutes before slicing. Store covered and eat within a sensible food-safe period.

name: Soft cinnamon swirl rolls
tip: A cosy weekend bake: allow time for two rises.
method: Warm the milk until lukewarm, not hot. Mix flour, yeast, caster sugar and a pinch of salt. Add milk, egg and 50 g softened butter; knead for 8–10 minutes until elastic. Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, then allow each rise to become visibly puffy before shaping or baking.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 60 minutes or until doubled in size.
Mix 30 g soft butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll dough to roughly 35 × 25 cm, spread the filling and roll up tightly from the long edge.
Cut into nine equal spirals. Arrange spaced slightly apart in a lined baking tin. Cover and rise for 35–45 minutes until visibly puffy.
Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Bake 22–27 minutes until golden and cooked through in the centres.
Cool for 10 minutes. Stir the icing sugar with 1–2 tsp water and drizzle over warm rolls.

name: No-knead rosemary focaccia
tip: Olive oil and a long rise give it the craggy, dimpled homemade top.
method: Mix strong white flour, yeast and 10 g fine salt in a large bowl. Add 400 ml lukewarm water and 30 ml olive oil and stir to a sticky dough. Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, then allow each rise to become visibly puffy before shaping or baking.
Cover and leave at room temperature for about 90 minutes until expanded and bubbly.
Oil a 23 × 33 cm baking tin with 25 ml olive oil. Tip dough in and gently fold it over itself once or twice with oiled fingers.
Stretch gently towards the corners. Cover and rest 35–45 minutes until puffy.
Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Drizzle over remaining 15 ml oil, dimple the surface with fingertips and scatter rosemary leaves and flaky sea salt.
Bake 23–28 minutes until deeply golden and cooked through. Rest about 10 minutes before cutting into nine pieces.

name: Rosemary lamb rump with creamy polenta and roast tomatoes
tip: A restaurant-style lamb dinner without a complicated sauce.

name: Beetroot and goat's cheese tart with walnut salad
tip: A flaky savoury tart with a sweet-sharp beetroot filling.

name: Prosciutto-wrapped chicken with sage butter and lemon beans
tip: Sage and lemon make simple chicken feel like a special supper.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Pat chicken breasts dry and check their thickness; flatten very thick ends for even cooking.
Lay two prosciutto slices overlapping around each chicken breast, tucking the ends under.

Return pan to gentle heat. Add butter, crushed garlic and torn sage leaves. Stir for 30 seconds, then add drained cannellini beans and stock, simmering 4–5 minutes until hot.
Fold in spinach until wilted. Finish with lemon zest and juice. Slice chicken and serve over the beans, spooning sage butter over the top.
